title: Numbers 1: Counting from One to Ten
titleRussian: Числа 1: считаем от одного до десяти
description: Meet the first ten Russian numbers as words. Today is pronunciation, recognition, and ordering. No grammar rules, no noun endings - just the sounds and shapes of один, два, три through десять.
descriptionRussian: Знакомимся с первыми десятью русскими числительными. Сегодня — произношение, узнавание и порядок. Никаких правил и окончаний, только сами слова: один, два, три и так до десяти.
intro: Ten words, and then the real subject of this book begins. Counting in Russian is not the hard part; every language makes you memorize ten sounds. The hard part is that a Russian number reaches over and changes the shape of the thing being counted, differently depending on which number it is. Today you learn the ten words with no consequences attached. From lesson 4 onward, each of them starts doing something to the noun beside it.
rules: The first ten Russian numbers are: один, два, три, четыре, пять, шесть, семь, восемь, девять, десять.
Numbers 5 through 10 all end in the soft sign -ь. Use that as a quick visual landmark.
Четыре is stressed on the second syllable: че-ТЫ-ре. The others are short enough that stress takes care of itself.
The question word сколько means 'how many'. You will pair it with numbers throughout this track.
Today is pure recognition. No noun endings change yet; that work starts in Lesson 2.
examples: Один (1). The first number; the only one Russian later treats like an adjective.
Три (3). Three letters, easy to read, easy to say.
Четыре (4). Three syllables, stress on the second: че-ТЫ-ре; the longest of the small numbers.
Пять (5). Single syllable; the soft -ь softens the т at the end.
Семь (7) and восемь (8). A natural pair: both end in -семь.
Десять (10). Closes the lesson; like 5-9, it ends in soft -ь.

items.hint: The number 5 ends in the soft sign -ь and has one syllable.
items.explanation: Пять is the Russian word for 5. It has one syllable and ends in the soft sign. From 5 to 10 every number ends in -ь, which is a useful visual landmark while you are learning the list.

items.hint: 8 pairs by sound with 7 (семь): both share the -семь shape.
items.explanation: Восемь is 8. It naturally pairs with семь (7): both end in the same syllable, so saying them together makes them easier to remember. Stress falls on the first syllable: ВО-семь.

items.hint: It is the longest small number, with three syllables.
items.explanation: Четыре is 4. It is the longest of the numbers from 1 to 10. Stress on the second syllable: че-ТЫ-ре. Knowing the stress now keeps it clean later, when you start putting nouns after it.
Между 'два' (2) и 'четыре' (4) стоит 'три' (3). The sequence один, два, три, четыре, пять is worth saying aloud until it flows like a song.
После 'девять' (9) идёт 'десять' (10). Both words end in -ять and share a similar rhythm, which is why they often get mixed up at first. Saying them as a pair (девять, десять) helps fix the order.

items.prompt: How many numbers are in today's lesson?
items.promptEnglish: How many numbers are in today's lesson?
items.explanation: Сегодняшний урок — это числа от 'один' до 'десять', всего десять чисел. From Lesson 2 onward, the question word 'сколько' (how many) will keep coming back.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The missing number in the sequence 1, 2, ?, 4, 5 is три (3). Today's lesson is pure recognition: read the sequence as a song until the words slot in by ear.

patternRecognition.question: Which number comes next?
patternRecognition.explanation: После 'восемь' (8) идёт 'девять' (9). The sequence rises by one each step: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10.

patternRecognition.question: Which number comes first?
patternRecognition.explanation: Перед 'два' (2) стоит 'один' (1). The counting list always opens with один; this is also the number you will start agreeing with nouns in Lesson 2.

patternRecognition.question: Which number is missing?
patternRecognition.explanation: Между 'семь' (7) и 'девять' (9) стоит 'восемь' (8). Семь и восемь — пара по звуку: оба слова кончаются на -семь.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort these numbers into 'small numbers' (1-4) and 'numbers ending in soft -ь' (5-10).

reviewVocab.definition: numeral (a counting word like один, два, пять; the building blocks of this whole track)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'пять' — это числительное, которое обозначает число 5.

reviewVocab.definition: digit (the written symbol 1, 2, 3; the visual side of the same idea)
how many / how much (a question word you will pair with numbers starting in Lesson 2)
reviewVocab.example: На вопрос 'Сколько?' можно ответить числом: один, два, три.
